optical-telescope.definition: A telescope built for astronomy gathers and records visible light from stars, planets, galaxies, and other distant objects in space.

reflecting-telescope.definition: An optical telescope that uses a large concave mirror to form an image, which its eyepiece enlarges.

refracting-telescope.definition: An optical telescope creates an image by bending incoming light through lenses and bringing it to a focus.

radio-telescope.definition: An astronomical instrument detects radio waves emitted by stars, galaxies, and other objects beyond Earth.
radio-telescope.exampleUsage: The radio telescope was used during the activity.

telescope-mount.definition: A mechanical support that holds a telescope and allows it to point accurately at different parts of the sky.
telescope-mount.exampleUsage: The telescope mount tracks the target smoothly.

eyepiece.definition: Combination of lenses at the viewing end of optical instruments.
eyepiece.exampleUsage: The eyepiece was used during the activity.

finder-scope.definition: A small auxiliary telescope with a wide field of view used to help aim a larger telescope.
finder-scope.exampleUsage: The astronomer used the finder scope to locate the star field.

lens.definition: A transparent optical device used to converge or diverge transmitted light and to form images.
lens.exampleUsage: The lens was used during the activity.

tripod.definition: A three-legged stand that keeps a camera steady.

star.definition: A luminous ball of hot gas that produces its own energy.

planet.definition: A large rounded object that orbits a star and does not produce its own light.

moon.definition: The natural satellite of the Earth.

sun.definition: The star that is the source of light and heat for the planets in the solar system.

comet.definition: (astronomy) a relatively small extraterrestrial body consisting of a frozen mass that travels around the sun in a highly elliptical orbit.

asteroid.definition: Any of numerous small celestial bodies composed of rock and metal that move around the sun (mainly between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter).

nebula.definition: A large cloud of gas and dust in space.

constellation.definition: A configuration of stars as seen from the earth.

meteor.definition: A streak of light in the sky at night that results when a meteoroid hits the earth's atmosphere and air friction causes the meteoroid to melt or vaporize or explode.

dome.definition: A stadium that has a roof.

rotating-roof.definition: A roof or dome structure that can turn so an opening can align with a telescope's viewing direction.
rotating-roof.exampleUsage: The observatory's rotating roof turned toward the target.

observation-deck.definition: An elevated platform designed to give visitors a clear view of the surrounding area or sky.
observation-deck.exampleUsage: Visitors gathered on the observation deck after sunset.

control-room.definition: A room where staff monitor and control a television broadcast.

computer-lab.definition: Designed to recreate a computer lab through its equipment, physical arrangement, and digital resources.

lecture-hall.definition: A large room at a school or college built for teaching many students at once.

gift-shop.definition: A retail shop offering a varied selection of items suitable for giving as presents.

parking-area.definition: An area set aside for leaving cars when their drivers are elsewhere.

pathway.definition: A bundle of myelinated nerve fibers following a path through the brain.

spectrograph.definition: An instrument that separates incoming light into a spectrum and records it.

ccd-camera.definition: A digital camera using a charge-coupled device sensor, commonly used for scientific imaging and astronomy.
ccd-camera.exampleUsage: The CCD camera recorded a long-exposure image of the galaxy.

star-chart.definition: A diagram maps the positions of stars within a selected region of the sky.

planetarium-projector.definition: A projector designed to display stars, planets, or other astronomical images on a planetarium dome.
planetarium-projector.exampleUsage: The planetarium projector displayed the night sky indoors.

computer-monitor.definition: A screen device that presents visual information sent from a computer.
computer-monitor.exampleUsage: The computer monitor was used during the activity.

data-server.definition: A computer system that stores, manages, or provides data to other computers over a network.
data-server.exampleUsage: The observatory stores image files on a data server.

laser-pointer.definition: A small device that produces a narrow laser beam used for pointing; lasers must never be aimed at eyes, people, vehicles, or aircraft.
laser-pointer.exampleUsage: The observatory follows strict safety rules for any laser pointer use.

red-flashlight.definition: A flashlight that produces red light, often used at night because it can be less disruptive to dark adaptation.
red-flashlight.exampleUsage: Visitors used dim red flashlights on the guided night tour.

logbook.definition: A book in which the log is written.

mercury.definition: The smallest planet and the nearest to the sun.

venus.definition: The second nearest planet to the sun.

mars.definition: A small reddish planet that is the 4th from the sun and is periodically visible to the naked eye.

jupiter.definition: The largest planet and the 5th from the sun.

saturn.definition: A giant planet that is surrounded by three planar concentric rings of ice particles.

uranus.definition: A giant planet with a ring of ice particles.

neptune.definition: A giant planet with a ring of ice particles.

pluto.definition: A dwarf planet in the outer Solar System beyond Neptune.

asteroid-belt.definition: A zone of the Solar System between Mars and Jupiter contains most of the asteroids identified so far.

star-gazing.definition: Looking at stars in the night sky.

data-analysis.definition: Careful examination of information reveals patterns, helps answer questions, and guides the conclusions people draw.

public-viewing.definition: An organized session in which members of the public observe the sky through observatory equipment.
public-viewing.exampleUsage: The observatory hosts supervised public viewing sessions.

night-tour.definition: A guided visit held at night, often to observe nighttime features or activities.
night-tour.exampleUsage: The night tour included a guided explanation of the telescope dome.

lecture.definition: A speech that is open to the public.

research.definition: Careful study done to find facts or answer a question.

sky-mapping.definition: The process of recording or displaying the positions of stars, galaxies, and other objects in the sky.
sky-mapping.exampleUsage: Students used software for a sky-mapping exercise.

eclipse-watching.definition: Observing an eclipse; a solar eclipse requires proper certified eye protection because looking directly at the Sun can cause permanent eye injury.
eclipse-watching.exampleUsage: The science program emphasized approved eye protection for eclipse watching.

meteor-shower.definition: A recurring sky display occurs when Earth crosses a comet’s debris trail, causing numerous meteors to glow as they burn in the atmosphere.

telescope.definition: An instrument that makes distant objects appear larger and easier to see.

camera.definition: Equipment for taking photographs (usually consisting of a lightproof box with a lens at one end and light-sensitive film at the other).

photometer.definition: Measuring instrument for measuring the luminous intensity of a source by comparing it (visually or photoelectrically) with a standard source.
photometer.exampleUsage: The photometer was used during the activity.

computer.definition: A machine for performing calculations automatically.
computer.exampleUsage: The computer was used during the activity.

antenna.definition: A device that sends or receives radio and television signals.
antenna.exampleUsage: The antenna was used during the activity.

magnitude.definition: A numerical measure of how bright a celestial object appears or actually is.

orbit.definition: An area in which something acts or operates or has power or control:.

light-year.definition: A unit of distance equal to how far light travels in a vacuum in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometers.
light-year.exampleUsage: The star is several light-years from Earth.

spectrum.definition: An ordered array of the components of an emission or wave.
spectrum.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Spectrum" in an educational description.

rotation.definition: The act of rotating as if on an axis.

eclipse.definition: An event in which one celestial object blocks light from another.

transit.definition: The passage of a celestial object across the apparent face of another.
transit.exampleUsage: The transit was used during the activity.
